126                                SANSKRIT GRAMMAR.               i § 911

ending in तृ and अक् and denoting the agent of the action; करत् 
सखा and not आत्मष्ठ; घटस्य कर्ता, ओदनस्य पाचकः &c.; but हृदश्वो
भक्षयामः स्तुकभक्षिका as the अक् here does not denote the agent.

Exception*:—But a compound is allowed in the case of the
words याजक one who employs as sacrificing priests, पूजक, परि-
चारक, परिवेषक a waiter at meals, स्नापक a servant who bathes
his master or brings bathing water for him, अध्यापक, उत्साहक
one who destroys, हैतृ, भर्तृ, when it does not mean 'a holder,'
and others not very important; ब्राह्मणयाजकः, देवपूजकः, राजपरि-
चारकः: &c.; अधिहोता, क्षमर्ती, &c. but वज्रस्य भर्तृ 'the thunder-
bolt-bearer'.

(b)† A specific Genitive (i.e. from which a singling out is 
made) is not compounded with any other words; as चूर्णो द्विजः श्रेष्ठः

(c)‡ A noun in the Genitive is not compounded with ordinal
numbers, words denoting qualities, words implying satisfaction
present participles, past participles meaning 'honoured or
approved of' or showing the place of the act, verbal indeclinables
and verbal nouns ending in तव्य; e.g. सर्वो पञ्चः, ब्राह्मणस्य शुक्लः
(हस्तः); काकस्य काण्येयः; फलानां शृद्धितः 'satisfied with fruits'.
(an Inst. Tat. is, of course, allowed in these cases); द्विजस्य कुर्वन्
कुर्वाणो वा किंचित्, सतां मतः esteemed by the good; राज्ञां पूजितः;
इदमेषां आसिति (place of sitting) गतो शुक्तं वा; ब्राह्मणस्य छात्रा, नृस्य
कर्तव्यम् &c.

* याजकादिभिश्च । Pāṇ. II. 2. 9
† न विधेयेन । Pāṇ. II. 2. 10.
‡ पूरणगुणसुहितार्थसत्व्यवतव्यमानाधिकरणैन । केन च पूजायाम् अधि-
करणशब्दिना च । Pāṇ. II. 2. 11-13. The prohibition with respect
to a word expressive of a quality (गुण) is not obligatory, remarks
Dikshita; as Pāṇ. himself uses such compounds as संज्ञाप्रमाणत्व
&c. Hence compounds like अर्थगौरवम्, बुद्धिमान्त्वम्, &c. are justi-
fied (अतिरोधे गुणेन निषेधः तदविषये संज्ञाप्रमाणत्वादित्वादिनिर्देशात् ।
तेनार्थगौरवं बुद्धिमान्त्वमित्यादि सिद्धम् ।).
